subject: Next steps: FinServCo eval plan & model recommendations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Smith <laura.smith@finservco.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@finservco.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up & action items from today’s discovery call — FinServCo eval plan

Hi Laura / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned on scope and success criteria for the eval you asked about: 

Summary of needs (as I heard them)
- Low-latency, high-accuracy extraction & classification across a range of financial documents (statements, loan apps, support chat).
- Strict PII handling and auditability for any hosted data.
- Need an objective, reproducible eval so Procurement & Security can sign off (SOC2 evidence + scoring).

Recommended models to include in the initial run
- redwood-7b-8k-quant (balanced cost / latency for conversational extraction)
- redwood-13b-16k (higher quality for long-form doc parsing)
- open-model-15b (baseline from model catalog for comparison)

Suggested eval plan & sizing
- Dataset: 1,000 curated examples across doc types (we recommend ~70% documents, 20% chat, 10% edge cases).
- Metric mix: exact-match for structured fields, token-level F1 for extraction spans, and a task-level human quality score for high-risk outputs.
- Pass/fail thresholds: we’ll propose initial gates but expect to iterate (example: structured field EM >= 92%, extraction F1 >= 0.88).

Data format & upload
- Preferred format: JSONL (one example per line). Required fields: id, input, expected, label_metadata (if applicable).
- I attached a template (finserv_eval_template.jsonl) and a short scoring doc (finserv_scoring_criteria.md).

Security & environment
- If you prefer not to upload PII to hosted endpoints we can run the eval in your Private deployment (VPC) or on Dedicated capacity. Please let me know your preference and we’ll provision the sandbox.

Next steps / owners
- Laura: confirm target dataset size (500-2000) and share sample (1-2 files) for format check — please upload to the shared folder or attach here.
- Marissa (me): prepare model variants and cost/time estimate, and share Redwood benchmark links and prompt sets.
- Neha (copied): scope the eval sandbox and estimate runtime + required GPU hours.

Timeline: we can kick off the sandbox and a first smoke run within 2 business days of receiving the sample dataset.

Links / references:
- Public benchmark we’ll use for baseline comparisons: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/finserv-2026
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-4321

Attachments: finserv_eval_template.jsonl, finserv_scoring_criteria.md

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up if helpful.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Laura Smith <laura.smith@finservco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@finservco.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & action items from today’s discovery call — FinServCo eval plan

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligns with our internal notes. A few quick clarifying Qs: 

1) PII & redaction: we plan to provide a redacted sample (attached) but will need the option for the eval to run in our VPC for any unredacted testing. Can you confirm the Private deployment option and what data access/granularity is available in that flow?

2) Scoring: the scoring doc you sent looks good. For the human quality score, can you share a short rubric for how Redwood rates outputs (1–5) so Procurement can review?

3) Timing & cost estimate: rough expected GPU hours for the 1,000-example run and an estimated cost bucket would be useful for budget/procurement.

I’ve attached a small redacted sample (finserv_sample_redacted.csv) to validate format. If the template you provided requires JSONL we can convert on our side but wanted to confirm acceptance of CSV samples for initial onboarding.

—
Laura Smith
Head of Data Products
FinServCo
laura.smith@finservco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Smith <laura.smith@finservco.com>, Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@finservco.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up & action items from today’s discovery call — FinServCo eval plan

Neha — forwarding Laura’s sample and questions. Can you take the lead on provisioning an eval sandbox (redwood eval sandbox) for FinServCo and run an initial smoke test with the following scope: 

Scope for smoke run (owner: Neha)
- Models to provision: redwood-7b-8k-quant, redwood-13b-16k, open-model-15b (catalog alias).
- Dataset: convert attached CSV sample to the recommended JSONL template (I attached finserv_eval_template.jsonl) — if conversion is straightforward you can do it; otherwise ask the customer to upload JSONL.
- Scoring: run EM and token F1 automated metrics + capture raw outputs for 100 examples. Also coordinate human rating pipeline for 100 sampled edge cases.
- Env: provision both a Hosted sandbox and a Private (VPC) sandbox estimate so Laura can choose. Include rough GPU hours and cost estimate for 1,000 examples (ballpark is fine).

Ask: can you confirm availability and milestone ETA? Ideally we’d have the hosted sandbox and an initial smoke run results within 48 hours of this note.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with the customer on dataset uploads.

—
Marissa
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Smith <laura.smith@finservco.com>, Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@finservco.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up & action items from today’s discovery call — FinServCo eval plan

Thanks Marissa — on it. Plan & initial estimates below: 

Provisioning plan
- I’ll spin up a Hosted eval sandbox in our staging region (us-west-2) and a Private VPC sandbox template for FinServCo to review.
- I’ll convert the attached CSV sample to JSONL using the standard script (fields: id, input, expected, metadata). I’ll post the converted sample to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cFinServEvalSandbox

Metrics & scoring
- Automated: exact match (structured), token F1 (span extraction), perplexity (if applicable).
- Human: 1–5 rubric for accuracy/harms/clarity (I attached a quick rubric to the Drive folder).

Estimate (ballpark)
- 1,000 examples, three models, single-pass eval (no human ratings): ~12 GPU hours on a small GPU pool (A100 equivalent) — estimate cost: $1,200–$1,800 depending on batching/quantization.
- Human rating pipeline (100 examples): 2–3 person-hours for setup + pay-per-rater costs (TBD).

ETA
- Hosted sandbox + converted sample uploaded to Drive: today EOD (I’ll confirm when done).
- Initial smoke run (100 examples) and summary: within 24–48 hours after sandbox is ready.

Next steps
- Laura/Tom: please confirm whether you’d like us to proceed with the Hosted sandbox or prefer the Private VPC template.
- Marissa: I’ll post the Drive link and a short results summary once the smoke run completes.

—
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
